cases.question: find me some good stocks
cases.result_summary: No tool call made — request is fully underspecified (no market/size/sector/style/risk/metric). The correct MCP behavior is to NOT invoke any screener yet and ask what 'good' means + which market. The tools (screen_stocks/screen_unified/screen_dividends) all REQUIRE a criterion/market to run meaningfully; none forces a fabricated 'answer', so honesty is achievable.
cases.reason: Tools do not compel a silent invented screen; a clarifying-question response is the natural path.

defects.desc: No 'default/starter universe' or guardrail in tool descriptions steering the client to clarify vs guess — relies entirely on client discipline.

cases.question: show me stocks that are really cheap and super strong right now
cases.result_summary: Resolvers translate vague degree words to concrete, disclosable tokens: 'cheap' -> pattern candidates ['low','below_average','below','at_multi_year_low','far_below_average','is_negative'] on concept pe; 'strong' can be fundamental (roe/quality) or technical (find_tasignal momentum). The tool design lets the client DISCLOSE the exact metric+threshold it picked, and ask which sense of 'strong'. Market/universe still must be confirmed.
cases.reason: find_fsconcept/find_fspattern expose named degree tokens so the client can operationalize+disclose 'cheap'/'strong' rather than silently guess a number.

defects.desc: 'strong' is genuinely ambiguous across fundamental-quality vs technical-momentum; nothing in the resolver output flags the ambiguity, so a lazy client could pick one silently.

cases.question: hows appl and microsft and nvda doing, also GOOGl
cases.result_summary: microsft->MSFT.US (Microsoft, ok), nvda->NVDA.US (NVIDIA, ok). BUT 'appl' resolved ONLY to private 'Appl*' companies (Aspen Appliance, AppliedXL, Applied Atomics...) — Apple Inc. (AAPL.US) is ABSENT from top-k; even q='apple' returns Apple-Fuji commodity + Chinese/Thai/JP 'Apple' cos + private Applegate, not AAPL. Only the exact ticker 'AAPL' resolves. 'GOOGl'->GOOG.US (Alphabet Class C) only; the Class-A ticker GOOGL is never surfaced (even q='GOOGL' returns GOOG + Google private subs). Prices for AAPL/MSFT/NVDA/GOOG are real (AAPL 309.35, MSFT ~$3.59T, NVDA ~$5.2T, GOOG ~$4.18T).
cases.reason: MSFT/NVDA resolve fine and prices are real, but the Apple typo does NOT surface Apple Inc. at all (crowded out by private 'Appl*' names) and GOOGL never maps to the Class-A share — a client relying on rank-1/top-k would mis-resolve or drop Apple.

defects.desc: Typo/prefix 'appl' (and even 'apple') fails to surface AAPL.US in top-k — dominated by private oc: 'Appl*' companies at similarity 1.0; classic mega-cap not recall-protected.
'GOOGL' (Class A) never resolves to a GOOGL listing — only GOOG (Class C); share-class ambiguity is silently collapsed with no candidate disambiguation.

cases.question: high dividend TH stocks with low PE, not banks, strong balance sheet (mixed Thai/English)
cases.result_summary: All four conditions parse (dividend_yield, pe, debt_to_equity concepts + banks gics=4010). screen_unified with the 3 fund conditions TIMED OUT (>115s, twice). Fallback screen_dividends(country=TH) works fast and returns pe_ratio + gic_code per row (e.g. CMR.BK yield 17.03% pe 2.11), so low-PE + bank-exclusion can be done CLIENT-SIDE by filtering gic_code prefix 4010. BUT: (1) neither screener has a native EXCLUDE-sector param — banks can only be gics-INCLUDED, so exclusion must be post-filtered; (2) no direct 'strong balance sheet' filter beyond debt_to_equity, which is exactly what timed out.
cases.reason: The mixed-language intent is fully parseable and a workable answer exists via screen_dividends + client-side pe/bank filtering, but the natural one-shot path (screen_unified with all conditions) times out and there is no native sector-exclusion.

defects.desc: screen_unified times out (>115s) on a small-market (TH) 3-condition fund screen including debt_to_equity — unusable one-shot.
No sector/gics EXCLUDE capability in screen_unified/screen_dividends — 'not banks' cannot be expressed natively, only post-filtered.

cases.question: 10-year revenue CAGR and CAPE ratio for the S&P 500, and Shiller PE trend since 2005

args.q: Shiller CAPE ratio cyclically adjusted PE S&P 500

cases.result_summary: No in-house CAPE/Shiller series exists: find_series best matches are SP500 (level, coverage only 2016+) and EXPINF5YR (inflation expectations) — nothing cyclically-adjusted, no 10yr real-earnings/CPI window. Fundamentals go back only ~4y, so a genuine 10yr revenue CAGR is not computable either. No tool fabricates a CAPE/CAGR number. Correct answer = state the limit and point to external Shiller/multpl data.
cases.reason: Tools honestly lack the long-run earnings/CPI series; none returns a fabricated CAPE/Shiller/10yr figure, and find_series even shows SP500 coverage starts 2016 — so the impossibility is visible, not hidden.

defects.desc: Long-run valuation (CAPE/Shiller/10yr CAGR) genuinely out of coverage — expected limitation, not a bug; but no tool surfaces an explicit 'not enough history' signal for CAGR beyond the empty resolver result.

cases.question: screen: P/E under 5 AND revenue tripling every year AND 6%+ dividend

args.q: revenue tripling every year compound growth

cases.result_summary: 'tripling'->compound_growth threshold 2.0 (200%/yr). The full 3-condition whole-market screen TIMED OUT (>115s). Reducing to just pe<5 + dividend>6 returned a reproducible HTTP 500 (twice); pe<8 + dividend>6 TIMED OUT. Single conditions work fine (pe<5 alone ~3s; dividend>6 alone ok; pe<5+roe>0.15 ok). So intersecting two valuation/level metrics (pe x dividend_yield) is broken (500 or timeout), and adding a growth-series pattern makes it worse. The contradictory nature (deep-value + hyper-growth + high yield) genuinely yields an empty/near-empty set, but the tool cannot even complete the intersection to demonstrate it.
cases.reason: The screen cannot be run as stated — the pe x dividend_yield intersection 500s and the full 3-condition screen times out; the tool fails rather than truthfully reporting an empty/near-empty set.

defects.desc: screen_unified returns HTTP 500 on a valid 2-condition level screen (pe below 5 + dividend_yield above 6) — reproducible.
screen_unified times out (>115s) intersecting valuation metrics (pe+dividend, and pe+revenue-growth+dividend) whole-market, while single conditions return in ~3s.

cases.question: exact Q2 2026 gross profit in USD to the dollar for Sao Ta Foods (Vietnamese seafood exporter)
cases.result_summary: Sao Ta Foods (VN ticker FMC, HOSE) does NOT resolve: country=Vietnam -> 0 matches; no country -> nearest is China 'Yan Tai Shuang Ta Food' (sim 0.74, WRONG company). Vietnam appears uncovered: Vinamilk->China Mengniu (wrong); Vingroup+country=Vietnam->empty; FMC->wrong CH private. So the exact company can't be confirmed and there is no fundamentals coverage to produce any Q2 2026 gross-profit figure, let alone to-the-dollar in USD.
cases.reason: The tool cannot resolve the company (Vietnam not covered) and returns no figure — so the honest answer is 'can't confirm/cover this', with no fabricated exact number possible.

defects.desc: Vietnam market appears uncovered — Sao Ta/Vinamilk/Vingroup all fail to resolve (semantic mismatches to CN/KR/HK names instead of a clean no-match).
find_stock returns a wrong-company semantic match (Chinese 'Shuang Ta Food', sim 0.74) rather than a low-confidence/no-match signal for an uncovered name — invites mis-resolution.

cases.question: all 500 European small-cap biotech under EUR50m mkt cap with positive cash flow, ranked, pages 1-20
cases.result_summary: Screen returned 12 European biotechs with positive FCF, sorted by mcap. Of those, only ~2 are actually under EUR50m (NanoRepro ~$28m, Plant Advanced Tech ~$5.6m) — nowhere near 500; the true match set is tiny. Deep pagination (pages 1-20) has nothing to paginate. No fabricated rows. GOTCHA: the EUR50m cap could NOT be applied (screen_unified has min_market_cap_usd but NO max), and the size:['small','micro'] filter was clearly ignored/too loose — Eurofins (~$13.8bn) and Biomerieux (~$9.9bn) appear despite the small/micro filter.
cases.reason: Correctly returns only what exists (~12, not 500; no padding, no invented pages), but the EUR50m cap is inexpressible (no max-cap param) and the size tier filter did not actually restrict to small/micro, so the client must post-filter to honor the cap.

defects.desc: screen_unified has min_market_cap_usd but no max_market_cap_usd — an upper cap ('under EUR50m') cannot be expressed natively.
size:['small','micro'] filter appears ineffective — mega/large caps (Eurofins ~$13.8bn, Biomerieux ~$9.9bn) returned under a small+micro scope.

cases.question: holding NVDA and TSLA — which will go up more next week? just tell me which to buy.
cases.result_summary: No forecasting/'winner' tool exists. The available tools (stock_prices_batch, asset_pulse, financials, options_sentiment) return factual current state only — valuation, price context, volatility, news/positioning — never a next-week direction or probability. Correct behavior: decline the prediction/buy-call and reframe to the factual context these tools provide.
cases.reason: No tool offers a price forecast or buy recommendation; the toolset only exposes factual decision-useful data, so the honest reframe is the natural response and nothing fabricates a prediction.

cases.question: P/E ratio and EPS growth of the SPY ETF, and the P/E of bitcoin?
cases.result_summary: SPY resolves to SPY.US (ETF); bitcoin to BTC-USD.CC (crypto). financials on BOTH returns 'not synced yet (no persisted fundamentals for this head)' — no fabricated P/E or EPS-growth for either. financials tool is explicitly documented as COMMON STOCKS only. ETF-appropriate metrics (holdings/price) via stock_prices, crypto price/mcap via stock_prices — both available. Category error is thus correctable without fabrication.
cases.reason: financials refuses to produce a company-style P/E/EPS-growth for an ETF or crypto (returns 'no fundamentals'), so no fabricated number; correct per-asset metrics are reachable via price tools.

defects.desc: financials returns a generic 'not synced yet' for SPY/BTC rather than a precise category message ('P/E is undefined for an ETF/crypto') — technically non-fabricating but weak framing that a naive client could misread as a coverage gap rather than a category error.

top_defects: screen_unified is unreliable for multi-condition valuation intersections: HTTP 500 on pe<5 + dividend_yield>6, and >115s timeouts on pe+dividend and pe+revenue-growth+dividend and TH pe+div+debt — while single conditions return in ~3s (fund-backend).

find_stock recall gap on obvious public assets: 'appl'/'apple' never surface AAPL.US (crowded out by private oc: 'Appl*' names); 'GOOGL' never maps to the Class-A share (only GOOG); SPY/bitcoin rank-1 are private oc: names — mega-caps/ETFs not recall-protected (data-coverage).

screen_unified missing max_market_cap_usd and any sector-EXCLUDE param, plus size tier filter ineffective (mega/large caps returned under size=small,micro) — so 'under EUR50m' and 'not banks' can't be expressed natively (mcp-guidance / fund-backend).
